topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture by framing the challenge and importance of studying complement within the immunology course.

topics.label: Fundamentals and core architecture of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental operating principles and molecular machinery of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three biochemical pathways through which complement recognizes pathogens to deposit C3b on target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three downstream effector mechanisms by which complement destroys pathogens and coordinates immune defense.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how host cells use regulatory proteins to prevent complement from attacking self-tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the distinct clinical presentations that arise when specific complement pathway components are deficient.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the strategies pathogens use to circumvent complement defenses, focusing on the example of Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and announces the topic of the upcoming lecture.
